title: Lie Algebras and Infinitesimal Group Schemes

items.title: The Lie algebra of a group scheme
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) with identity point $e=e_G\in G(k)$. Let $\mathfrak m_e=\ker(\varepsilon:\mathcal O_{G,e}\to k)$ be the maximal ideal of the local ring of $G$ at $e$ and let $T_{G/k,e}=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2,k)$ be the tangent space of $G$ over $k$ at $e$ ([[def-relative-cotangent-space]], [[thm-cotangent-space-maximal-ideal-quotient]]). The **Lie algebra of $G$** is $\operatorname{Lie}(G):=T_{G/k,e}$, written $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. By [[thm-tangent-vectors-dual-numbers]] the tangent space is canonically the set of $k$-morphisms $\tau:\operatorname{Spec}k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\to G$ whose composite with $\varepsilon\mapsto0$ is $e$, that is, $\operatorname{Lie}(G)\cong\ker\bigl(G(k[\varepsilon])\to G(k)\bigr)$; for a commutative $k$-algebra $R$ one writes $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R):=\ker\bigl(G(R[\varepsilon])\to G(R)\bigr)$ with $R[\varepsilon]=R\otimes_k k[\varepsilon]$, and the elements are written $e^{\varepsilon X}$. The vector-space structure, the naturality of these identifications and their agreement with the cotangent description are proved in [[lem-lie-algebra-tangent-space-and-functoriality]], which is the well-definedness statement for this definition. No affineness, reducedness, smoothness, or characteristic hypothesis is imposed, and $G$ need not be affine.
items.strategy: Definition: take the tangent space at the identity as the Lie algebra and record the two descriptions (dual of the cotangent space, and dual-number points reducing to $e$) fixed by the published tangent-space theorems; the identity $e$ is a $k$-rational point, so those theorems apply. The vector-space structure and functoriality are deliberately not asserted here; they are the content of the referenced lemma.

items.title: The tangent space at the identity is a vector space, and Lie is a functor
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ ([[def-lie-algebra-of-a-group-scheme]]). (a) For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the set $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)=\ker(G(R[\varepsilon])\to G(R))$ is an abelian group under the multiplication of $G(R[\varepsilon])$; this multiplication is addition for a natural $R$-module structure on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)$, and there is a natural $R$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)\cong\mathfrak g\otimes_kR$. In particular $\mathfrak g$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and the bijections of [[def-lie-algebra-of-a-group-scheme]] with $\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2,k)$ and with the dual-number points are isomorphisms of $k$-vector spaces. (b) A morphism $f:G\to H$ of group schemes of finite type over $k$ induces a $k$-linear map $\operatorname{Lie}(f):\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak h$, with $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{id})=\operatorname{id}$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(g\circ f)=\operatorname{Lie}(g)\circ\operatorname{Lie}(f)$, and $f_R(e^{\varepsilon X})=e^{\varepsilon\operatorname{Lie}(f)_R(X)}$ for $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)$. If $f$ is a closed immersion ([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]) then $\operatorname{Lie}(f)$ is injective. The proof makes only finite selections and uses no choice principle.
items.strategy: Direct. (a) The multiplication of $G(R[\varepsilon])$ restricts to the kernel of the reduction; it is commutative because the induced map of tangent spaces in the first variable is the identity by $m\circ(\operatorname{id},e)=\operatorname{id}$ and in the second by $m\circ(e,\operatorname{id})=\operatorname{id}$, and the induced maps are additive, so $(X,Y)\mapsto X+Y$. Scalar multiplication comes from the $k$-algebra endomorphism $\varepsilon\mapsto c\varepsilon$ of $k[\varepsilon]$ (functoriality in $R$). Base change to $R$ gives $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)\cong T_{G_R/R,e_R}\cong\operatorname{Lie}(G)\otimes_kR$ by [[lem-differentials-commute-base-change-schemes]] together with the naturality in [[thm-tangent-vectors-dual-numbers]], and finite-dimensionality follows because $\mathcal O_{G,e}$ is Noetherian, so $\mathfrak m_e$ is finitely generated. (b) Functoriality is the naturality of the tangent-space identification, and the exponential identity is its dual-number form; a closed immersion is a monomorphism, so its map on dual-number points reducing to the identity is injective.

items.title: The adjoint representation of an affine group scheme
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ ([[def-lie-algebra-of-a-group-scheme]]). (a) For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $x\in G(R)$, conjugation $y\mapsto xyx^{-1}$ in $G(R[\varepsilon])$ restricts to an $R$-linear automorphism $\operatorname{Ad}(x)$ of $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)=\mathfrak g\otimes_kR$, and $x\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}(x)$ is a natural homomorphism of groups; under the identification $\operatorname{Lie}(G)(R)\cong\mathfrak g\otimes_kR$ it is a natural transformation $h_G\to h_{\operatorname{GL}_{\mathfrak g}}$, hence a morphism of $k$-group schemes $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathfrak g}$, the **adjoint representation** of $G$. (b) For all $x\in G(R)$ and $X\in\mathfrak g\otimes_kR$ one has $x\,e^{\varepsilon X}\,x^{-1}=e^{\varepsilon\operatorname{Ad}(x)X}$ in $G(R[\varepsilon])$. (c) For a morphism $f:G\to H$ of affine group schemes of finite type over $k$ and all $x\in G(R)$ one has $\operatorname{Ad}_H(f(x))\circ\operatorname{Lie}(f)=\operatorname{Lie}(f)\circ\operatorname{Ad}_G(x)$; equivalently, $\operatorname{Ad}$ is natural in $G$.
items.strategy: Conjugation by $x\in G(R)$ is an automorphism of the group $G(R[\varepsilon])$ that preserves the kernel $\mathfrak g\otimes_kR$, and clause (b) defines $\operatorname{Ad}(x)X$; additivity and $R$-linearity in $X$ follow from the exponential identities of [[lem-lie-algebra-tangent-space-and-functoriality]] applied to the products, and multiplicativity and naturality in $R$ are immediate from the functoriality of the group law. Choosing a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak g$ identifies $\operatorname{GL}_{\mathfrak g}$ with the general linear group scheme of [[lem-general-linear-group-scheme-and-its-coordinate-ring]], so the natural transformation is induced by a morphism of affine schemes by [[thm-affine-schemes-determined-by-functor-of-points]] and [[thm-yoneda-lemma-is-natural-in-both-variables]]. Clause (c) follows by applying the functoriality of the exponential correspondence to the identity of (b) and comparing at the identity of $H$.

items.title: The Lie algebra of the general linear group
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge1$. Under the identification $\operatorname{GL}_n=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_{ij},d^{-1}]$ of [[lem-general-linear-group-scheme-and-its-coordinate-ring]], the tangent space at the identity is $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{GL}_n)\cong M_n(k)=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, the isomorphism sending a matrix $X$ to the dual-number point $I_n+\varepsilon X$; in particular $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_m)\cong k$ for $n=1$, generated by the class of $x_{11}-1$ (equivalently of $t-1$). For matrices $X,Y$ the commutator of the lifts $I+\varepsilon X$ and $I+\varepsilon'Y$ in $\operatorname{GL}_n\bigl(k[t,t']/(t^2,t'^2)\bigr)$ is $I+tt'(XY-YX)$, and the adjoint representation of [[lem-adjoint-representation-of-an-affine-group-scheme]] satisfies $\operatorname{Ad}(A)X=AXA^{-1}$ for all commutative $k$-algebras $R$, $A\in\operatorname{GL}_n(R)$ and $X\in M_n(R)$.
items.strategy: Compute in the coordinate ring $k[x_{ij},d^{-1}]$: the augmentation is $x_{ij}\mapsto\delta_{ij}$, so the augmentation ideal is generated by the elements $x_{ij}-\delta_{ij}$ and their classes form a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2$, while $d$ maps to a unit; this gives $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{GL}_n)\cong M_n(k)$ with inverse map $X\mapsto I+\varepsilon X$. Expanding the product $(I+\varepsilon X)(I+\varepsilon'Y)(I-\varepsilon X)(I-\varepsilon'Y)$ and using $\varepsilon^2=(\varepsilon')^2=0$ gives $I+\varepsilon\varepsilon'(XY-YX)$; the adjoint formula is the same conjugation computation on dual-number points.

items.title: The Lie bracket from infinitesimals and the adjoint action
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ and adjoint representation $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathfrak g}$ ([[lem-adjoint-representation-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). (a) The differential $\operatorname{ad}:=\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{Ad}):\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak g)$ is $k$-linear and $[X,Y]:=\operatorname{ad}(X)(Y)$ makes $\mathfrak g$ a Lie algebra over $k$ ([[def-lie-algebra-over-a-field]]), with $\operatorname{ad}(X)$ a derivation of $\mathfrak g$ for every $X$ ([[def-derivation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). (b) The bracket is functorial: for a morphism $f:G\to H$ of affine group schemes of finite type over $k$, the map $\operatorname{Lie}(f):\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak h$ is a homomorphism of Lie algebras. (c) For $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$, in $G\bigl(k[t,t']/(t^2,t'^2)\bigr)$ one has $e^{tX}e^{t'Y}e^{-tX}e^{-t'Y}=e^{tt'[X,Y]}$, where $X,Y$ are regarded in $\mathfrak g\otimes_kk[t,t']/(t^2,t'^2)$ through the two factors; equivalently, $[X,Y]$ is the unique element of $\mathfrak g$ whose image under the ring map $k[\varepsilon]\to k[t,t']/(t^2,t'^2)$, $\varepsilon\mapsto tt'$, is the commutator of the two dual-number lifts. (d) If $G=\operatorname{GL}_n$ then $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ under the identification $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$ of [[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-general-linear-group]]. (e) A closed immersion of affine group schemes of finite type over $k$ induces an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras; consequently two bracket assignments on the Lie algebras of affine group schemes of finite type over $k$ which are functorial in $G$ and give the matrix commutator on $\operatorname{GL}_n$ agree. The Axiom of Choice is used only in (e), through the faithful finite-dimensional representation theorem [[thm-affine-group-scheme-faithful-finite-dimensional-representation]].
items.strategy: Define $\operatorname{ad}=\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{Ad})$ and $[X,Y]=\operatorname{ad}(X)Y$. Clause (b) follows from the naturality of $\operatorname{Ad}$ (clause (c) of the adjoint-representation lemma) and of $\operatorname{Lie}$ by differentiating $\operatorname{Ad}_H(f(x))\operatorname{Lie}(f)=\operatorname{Lie}(f)\operatorname{Ad}_G(x)$ at the identity. Clause (c) follows from $x\,e^{\varepsilon Y}x^{-1}=e^{\varepsilon\operatorname{Ad}(x)Y}$ with $x=e^{tX}$ and $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{tX})=\operatorname{id}+t\operatorname{ad}(X)$ modulo $t^2$, using additivity of the exponential correspondence. Antisymmetry is obtained from (c) by comparing the two commutators, which are inverse to each other; Jacobi follows by applying (b) to $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathfrak g}$ and using the matrix case (d): $\operatorname{ad}([X,Y])=[\operatorname{ad}X,\operatorname{ad}Y]=\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y-\operatorname{ad}Y\operatorname{ad}X$, which applied to $Z$ is the Jacobi identity and shows $\operatorname{ad}(X)\in\operatorname{Der}(\mathfrak g)$. Clause (d) is [[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-general-linear-group]]. Clause (e): injectivity of $\operatorname{Lie}$ on closed immersions is [[lem-lie-algebra-tangent-space-and-functoriality]], the faithful representation exists by [[thm-affine-group-scheme-faithful-finite-dimensional-representation]], and functoriality forces the bracket on $\mathfrak g$ to be the pullback of the matrix commutator along an injection, hence determines it.

items.title: Invariant differentials and the cotangent space at the identity
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ with structure morphism $f:G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and identity $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_G$-modules $\Omega_{G/k}\cong f^*e^*\Omega_{G/k}$ (the module of invariant differentials), and $e^*\Omega_{G/k}\cong\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2$ is the cotangent space of $G$ at the identity. Consequently $\Omega_{G/k}\cong\mathcal O_G\otimes_k(\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2)$ is a free $\mathcal O_G$-module of rank $\dim_k\operatorname{Lie}(G)$; moreover, for every $k$-rational point $x\in G(k)$, left translation by $x$ identifies the cotangent space $\Omega_{G/k}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{G,x}}\kappa(x)$ with $\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2$.
items.strategy: Follow the shearing-automorphism proof of Stacks 39.6.3, valid for group schemes over any base. View $G\times_kG$ as a $G$-scheme through the second projection; by [[lem-differentials-commute-base-change-schemes]] applied to the base change of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ along itself, $\Omega_{G\times_kG/G}\cong\operatorname{pr}_0^*\Omega_{G/k}$ for the first projection $\operatorname{pr}_0$. The shearing map $\tau(g,h)=(m(g,h),h)$ is an automorphism of $G\times_kG$ over the second projection, with inverse $(u,h)\mapsto(m(u,i(h)),h)$ built from multiplication and inversion; pulling the base-change isomorphism back along $\tau$ gives $m^*\Omega_{G/k}\cong\operatorname{pr}_0^*\Omega_{G/k}$, and pulling back along $(e\circ f,\operatorname{id}_G):G\to G\times_kG$ gives $\Omega_{G/k}\cong f^*e^*\Omega_{G/k}$. The identification of $e^*\Omega_{G/k}$ with $\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2$ is [[thm-cotangent-space-maximal-ideal-quotient]] at the $k$-rational point $e$, and freeness follows because a quasicoherent sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a $k$-vector space.

items.title: A differential generating a free direct summand is a nonzerodivisor
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $S$ a nonzero $\mathbb Q$-algebra, and let $f\in S$. Assume that there is an $S$-linear map $\theta:\Omega_{S/R}\to S$ with $\theta(\mathrm df)=1$; equivalently, $S\,\mathrm df$ is freely generated by $\mathrm df$ and $\Omega_{S/R}=S\,\mathrm df\oplus C$ for an $S$-submodule $C$ (then $\theta$ is projection onto this free summand and $C=\ker\theta$). Then $f$ is not nilpotent, and if $S$ is a Noetherian local ring then $f$ is a nonzerodivisor. No finiteness of $S$ over $R$ is assumed. The Axiom of Choice is used only through the Krull intersection theorem in the nonzerodivisor statement.
items.strategy: Define the $R$-derivation $D:S\to S$ by $D(a)=\theta(\mathrm da)$; then $D(f)=1$ and $D(f^n)=nf^{n-1}$ by the Leibniz rule, so $f^n=0$ with $n>1$ minimal would give $nf^{n-1}=0$, contradicting minimality because $n$ is a unit of $S$. For the nonzerodivisor statement suppose $fa=0$; then $0=D(fa)=fD(a)+a$, so $a\in(f)$, and if $a=f^nb$ then $0=D(f^{n+1}b)=(n+1)f^nb+f^{n+1}D(b)$ gives $a\in(f^{n+1})$; the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring is contained in its Jacobson radical, so $\bigcap_n(f^n)=0$ by [[thm-krull-intersection-theorem]], whence $a=0$.

items.title: Free differentials imply regularity in characteristic zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $A$ be a finite-type $k$-algebra and let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$. If $\Omega_{A/k,\mathfrak q}$ is a free $A_{\mathfrak q}$-module, then $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring. No bound on the rank and no smoothness of $A$ is assumed. (The statement fails in characteristic $p>0$: $A=k[t]/(t^p)$ at the origin has free rank-one differentials but a nonregular local ring.)
items.strategy: Induction on $d=\dim A_{\mathfrak q}$ following Stacks 10.140.7. Put $R=A_{\mathfrak q}$, $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Since $k$ has characteristic $0$ it is perfect, so by [[thm-ag-separating-transcendence-basis-perfect-field]] the finitely generated field extension $\kappa/k$ is separably generated and the injection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\hookrightarrow\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa$ of [[lem-ag-separable-residue-cotangent-sequence]] is available. If $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=0$ then $R$ is a field and regular. Otherwise pick $f\in\mathfrak m$ with nonzero class; the injection makes the image of $\mathrm df$ in $\Omega_{R/k}/\mathfrak m\Omega_{R/k}$ nonzero, so by [[cor-minimal-generators-over-a-local-ring]] the element $\mathrm df$ extends to a minimal generating set of the finite free module $\Omega_{R/k}$, whose image in $\Omega_{R/k}/\mathfrak m\Omega_{R/k}$ is a $\kappa$-basis; a surjection of finite free $R$-modules of equal rank is injective because $R$ is Noetherian and a Noetherian module is Hopfian ([[cor-noetherian-modules-are-hopfian]]), so this generating set is a basis and there is an $R$-linear $\theta$ with $\theta(\mathrm df)=1$. Then $f$ is a nonzerodivisor by [[lem-differentials-generating-a-free-direct-summand-are-nonzerodivisors]], and the conormal sequence $\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R(R/fR)\to\Omega_{(R/fR)/k}\to0$ of [[thm-conormal-exact-sequence-algebra]] exhibits $\Omega_{(R/fR)/k}$ as free of rank one less; by [[thm-quotient-and-lifting-regularity-across-a-regular-element]] $\dim R/fR=\dim R-1$, so the induction hypothesis makes $R/fR$ regular, and the same item lifts regularity to $R$. The characteristic hypothesis enters only through the nonzerodivisor step.

items.title: Smoothness over a characteristic-zero field via free differentials
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $X$ be a $k$-scheme locally of finite type ([[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]). If $\Omega_{X/k}$ is locally free ([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]]), then $X$ is smooth over $k$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]). Conversely, if $X$ is smooth over $k$ then $\Omega_{X/k}$ is locally free of finite rank ([[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]]); over a characteristic-zero field the two conditions are therefore equivalent. The Axiom of Choice is used through the cited regularity and Jacobian results.
items.strategy: Work at a point $x\in X$ with an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of finite type over $k$ and prime $\mathfrak q$; local freeness of $\Omega_{X/k}$ makes $\Omega_{A/k,\mathfrak q}$ free, so $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular by [[lem-free-differentials-imply-regular-in-characteristic-zero]]. Since a field of characteristic $0$ is perfect, clause 2 of [[thm-ag-perfect-field-jacobian-regularity]] gives $t\notin\mathfrak q$ with $A_t$ standard smooth over $k$ ([[def-ag-standard-smooth-algebra]]); by clause 1 of [[thm-ag-standard-smooth-geometric-regularity]] the structure morphism is flat at $\mathfrak q$ with geometrically regular fibre. A finitely generated algebra over the Noetherian field $k$ is finitely presented by [[cor-finite-type-algebra-over-noetherian-ring-is-finitely-presented]], so $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation and hence smooth at $x$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]); as $x$ was arbitrary, $X$ is smooth. The converse is [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]].

items.title: Cartier's theorem: affine group schemes in characteristic zero are smooth
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]). Then the structure morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, that is, $G$ is a smooth group scheme over $k$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]). In particular every local ring $\mathcal O_{G,g}$ is regular and $G$ is reduced. No smoothness, reducedness or finiteness of $G$ beyond finite type is assumed, and the characteristic-zero hypothesis is essential: in characteristic $p>0$ the finite group schemes $\alpha_p$ and $\mu_p$ are not smooth.
items.strategy: By [[lem-invariant-differentials-of-a-group-scheme]] the module $\Omega_{G/k}$ is free, hence locally free; [[thm-smoothness-over-characteristic-zero-via-free-differentials]] then makes the locally finite type morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ smooth. Smoothness at $g$ means the fibre over $\kappa(\operatorname{Spec}k)=k$, namely $G$ itself, is geometrically regular at $g$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-ag-geometrically-regular-algebra-and-fibre]]), so applying the condition to the trivial field extension $k/k$ gives that $\mathcal O_{G,g}$ is regular; a regular local ring is a domain ([[lem-regular-local-domain-induction]]), whence $G$ is reduced. Milne's independent Oort-style nilpotent proof (M22 Lemma 3.19, Lemma 3.20, Lemma 3.22 and Theorem 3.23) and Stacks 39.8.2 are recorded as alternative complete treatments in the coverage file; the local proof above is the one used. In positive characteristic $\alpha_p$ has free differentials but a nonregular local ring, so the hypothesis cannot be dropped.

title: Lie Algebras and Infinitesimal Group Schemes — Examples

items.title: Additive and infinitesimal group schemes
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field. (a) $\mathbf G_a=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ with comultiplication $\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+1\otimes t$, counit $\varepsilon(t)=0$ and antipode $S(t)=-t$ is a group scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. (b) If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then $\alpha_p=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]/(t^p)$, with the comultiplication induced by that of $\mathbf G_a$, is a closed subgroup scheme of $\mathbf G_a$ with $\alpha_p(R)=\{a\in R:a^p=0\}$, and $\mu_p=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]/(t^p-1)$, with the comultiplication of the multiplicative group scheme ([[lem-general-linear-group-scheme-and-its-coordinate-ring]]), is a closed subgroup scheme of $\mathbf G_m$ with $\mu_p(R)=\{a\in R^\times:a^p=1\}$. The coordinate rings of $\alpha_p$ and $\mu_p$ are isomorphic to $k[s]/(s^p)$ for $s=t$ respectively $s=t-1$, so both are finite nonreduced $k$-schemes of length $p$, while $\mathbf G_a$ and $\mathbf G_m$ are reduced.
items.strategy: Direct computations with the explicit algebra maps. On $k[t]$ the map $t\mapsto t\otimes1+1\otimes t$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism satisfying the coassociativity and counit identities, and $t\mapsto-t$ is an antipode; on $k[t]/(t^p)$ it is well defined because $(t\otimes1+1\otimes t)^p=t^p\otimes1+1\otimes t^p$ in characteristic $p$ (all intermediate binomial coefficients are divisible by $p$), so $(t^p)$ is a Hopf ideal and [[lem-hopf-ideal-kernels-and-quotients]] gives the quotient Hopf structure; on $k[t,t^{-1}]/(t^p-1)$ the formulas $t\mapsto t\otimes t$ and $t\mapsto t^{-1}$ are well defined because $t^p=1$ forces $(t\otimes t)^p=1$. Group-object identities are checked on the algebra generators, and the point descriptions follow by evaluating the coordinate rings. The nonzero nilpotent $s$ exhibits nonreducedness and the length is $p$ because $1,s,\dots,s^{p-1}$ is a $k$-basis.

items.title: Lie algebras of the additive, infinitesimal and general linear groups
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $\operatorname{Lie}$ be as in [[def-lie-algebra-of-a-group-scheme]]. (a) $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_a)\cong k$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_m)\cong k$, generated by the classes of $t$ and of $t-1$ in $\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2$; the bracket is zero because these groups are abelian, so the Lie algebras are the one-dimensional abelian Lie algebras. (b) If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then $\operatorname{Lie}(\alpha_p)\cong k$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(\mu_p)\cong k$ with the same generators, so there are isomorphisms of $k$-Lie algebras $\operatorname{Lie}(\alpha_p)\cong\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_a)$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(\mu_p)\cong\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_m)$. (c) $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{GL}_n)=\mathfrak{gl}_n=M_n(k)$, the isomorphism sending $X$ to $I+\varepsilon X$, and $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ ([[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-general-linear-group]], [[thm-lie-bracket-and-adjoint-action-from-infinitesimals]]).
items.strategy: Compute the cotangent space at the identity from the coordinate rings. For $k[t]$ and $k[t,t^{-1}]$ the augmentation ideals are generated by $t$ respectively $t-1$, whose classes form a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2$ ([[thm-cotangent-space-maximal-ideal-quotient]]). For $k[s]/(s^p)$ the same class is a basis: $s^p=0$ lies in $\mathfrak m_e^2$ while $s$ does not, for $p\ge2$. Every one-dimensional Lie algebra has zero bracket because $[X,X]=0$ and $X$ generates; this applies to $\mathbf G_a$, $\mathbf G_m$, $\alpha_p$ and $\mu_p$, all of which are commutative as group schemes, so functoriality of the bracket also gives zero directly. Clause (c) is [[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-general-linear-group]] together with clause (d) of [[thm-lie-bracket-and-adjoint-action-from-infinitesimals]].

items.title: The Lie algebra does not detect nonsmooth group schemes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$. The closed subgroup scheme $\alpha_p\subseteq\mathbf G_a$ of [[ex-additive-and-infinitesimal-group-schemes]] is a finite nonreduced group scheme of order $p$ over $k$ which is not smooth over $k$, whereas $\mathbf G_a$ is smooth over $k$; nevertheless $\operatorname{Lie}(\alpha_p)\cong\operatorname{Lie}(\mathbf G_a)$ as $k$-Lie algebras ([[ex-lie-algebras-of-alpha-p-mu-p-and-gl-n]]). The same contrast holds between $\mu_p$ and $\mathbf G_m$. Consequently the Lie algebra of a group scheme of finite type over a field does not determine smoothness, so it is not a complete invariant of the infinitesimal structure. The Axiom of Choice is used only through the cited regularity, domain and standard-smoothness suppliers.
items.strategy: Non-smoothness of $\alpha_p$: its coordinate ring $k[s]/(s^p)$ has the nonzero nilpotent $s$, so $\alpha_p$ is finite of length $p$ and not reduced. If it were smooth at its origin, then the fibre condition in [[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], applied with the trivial field extension $k/k$ as in [[def-ag-geometrically-regular-algebra-and-fibre]] and [[def-regular-local-ring-geometric-point]], would make the local ring $k[s]/(s^p)_{(s)}$ regular; a regular local ring is a domain by [[lem-regular-local-domain-induction]], contradicting $s\ne0$ with $s^p=0$. Smoothness of $\mathbf G_a$: $k[t]$ is standard smooth over $k$ ([[def-ag-standard-smooth-algebra]]) and is finitely presented over the Noetherian field $k$ ([[cor-finite-type-algebra-over-noetherian-ring-is-finitely-presented]]), so $\mathbf G_a$ is smooth over $k$ by [[thm-ag-standard-smooth-geometric-regularity]] and [[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]; the same argument applies to $\mathbf G_m=k[t,t^{-1}]$. The isomorphism of Lie algebras is [[ex-lie-algebras-of-alpha-p-mu-p-and-gl-n]], and the $\mu_p$ case is identical with $s=t-1$.
